why: The fixed input of the agent suite (A1-lite): which 40 WebVoyager tasks, the agent's and the judge's prompts, the models and every cap. run.py records the sha256 of this file in env.json. Nothing here is random: the ids are what `agent_rules.select` makes of the pinned data and the published seed, and the suite refuses to start when they differ.

source.note: WebVoyager tasks with dates moved ahead, the 55 impossible ids browser-use dropped, and the reference answers. The pool is 643 - 55 = 588 tasks (browser-use quotes 586).

method: 40 over 15 sites: 2 per site, and the 10 left over go to the 10 sites that rank first by sha256(seed|'site|'+site); inside a site the tasks that rank first by sha256(seed|'task|'+id); run order = rank by sha256(seed|'order|'+id).

agent.prompt:
Start at {web} and answer this question using only what you read on the web: {ques}
Do not log in, buy, post or submit anything. Finish with one last line: ANSWER: <your answer, short and exact>.

kinds.possible: true on the day the task was written; the live page may differ now

evidence.why: What the judge is shown. All the text of the worked calls that show a page when it fits in `chars`; else the lines (cut to `line_chars`, with the line before and after) that hold a number or a 4+-letter word of the answer, most distinct first, then the last `pages` read or view pages cut to `page_chars` as far as room is left. Before all of that, in full up to `chars`: the pages whose address or arXiv id the answer cites. `fill` and `script` are left out: their text is the agent's own input. Plus the last `screenshots` images, sent as image blocks.

judge.votes_why: Three votes on the same prompt; a pass needs at least 2 SUCCESS, and a vote with no verdict is not a SUCCESS. The row keeps the votes and how many agree.

caps.why: At most 40 tasks x 1 run, plus at most 3 reruns of a task whose attempt failed for a model or infra reason, capped at 80 agent runs in all (40 reruns); three judge votes per completed task (120), plus reruns of a vote that hit an API error or gave no verdict, capped at 160. Worst case 240 CLI runs and 80 x 25 = 2000 agent turns.

redate.rule: Move every date in the question by the same whole number of years N, the smallest N for which the earliest date is at least 30 days after the run date (UTC); a re-dated task's reference becomes `possible`. `agent_rules.redate`; `summarize.check` re-applies it. The suite refuses to start when the dates it finds in the 40 questions are not these.

references.why: A reference that contradicts a condition its own task states, found by reading all 40. For these the deterministic check is skipped and the judge is shown 'none: <reason>' in place of the reference. Placeholder references (`<model 1>`, `<summary>`) do not contradict their task and are not listed.

broken.Allrecipes--5: asks for >1000 reviews; the reference has 818

not_doable.Allrecipes--32: HTTP 402 IP block on every page, in both runs of 2026-10-11
not_doable.Allrecipes--5: HTTP 402 IP block on every page, in both runs of 2026-10-11

not_doable_why: Fixed before the run: tasks no rule shows doable from the bench's address today. The summary prints the raw number, then the number without these, then the number without these and the bot-walled ones. Geo tasks (Amazon, Booking, Google Flights, Google Maps) are not listed: Sonnet passed Amazon--26 and Google Map--19, so no rule proves them dead.
